Emma (Finance): Hey team — saw an invoice from last month where ACME Corp shows reserved commit usage but also a large burst line for the same UTC window (2026-02-18 02:00-03:00). Looks like double billing. Anyone else see this?
Luke (Billing): ugh, I see it. invoice INV-2026-0412 line 7 = reserved commit allocation, line 9 = burst charge for same nodepool.
Sana (CS): I remember we had a planned failover for ACME to eu-west for a 20m window that day. Could be failover + burst overlap.
Mike (Ops): Checking serving logs and failover events now. If failover triggered, we should have metering tags: region=eu-west and failover=true.
billing-bot: Detected potential duplicate meter tags on invoice INV-2026-0412. Suggested action: reconcile reserved vs burst usage.
Emma (Finance): Can we pull the metering export for that nodepool (np-acme-prod-1) for the window 02:00-03:30 UTC? Need to confirm whether tokens were billed under both reserved bucket and burst.
Mike (Ops): grabbing logs — exporting now. snippet shows request ids routed to failover pool and also counted against reserved pool due to sticky hashing bug.
Mike (Ops): ```
# metering excerpt
2026-02-18T02:07:12Z np-acme-prod-1 reserved_bucket tokens=12,345
2026-02-18T02:07:12Z np-acme-prod-1 failover-burst tokens=12,345
```
Nora (AcctMgr): If that's true, ACME will escalate. They already pinged their finance team. We should propose an SLA credit and provisional refund while we investigate.
Luke (Billing): Agree. What's the estimated overcharge amount? Emma, can you estimate?
Emma (Finance): Preliminary calc: duplicated tokens ≈ 12,345 => ~$98. Add billing rounding/tax -> request provisional credit of $120.
Sana (CS): We should also flag the serving runtime fix (sticky hashing) in internal backlog. Ops, is there a patch ETA?
Mike (Ops): Hotfix deployed to nodepool selector yesterday morning (2026-02-19 09:15 UTC). Root cause: replica routing table didn't drop failover tag on retry. Patch GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2426.
Emma (Finance): OK. Proposed plan: 1) Apply provisional credit $120 to ACME invoice INV-2026-0412, 2) Follow up with final reconciled amount after full metering audit, 3) Offer 1 week of waived burst charges (goodwill) if ACME wants. Approve?
Luke (Billing): I can process provisional credit but need approval from finance director. Tagging Nora.
Nora (AcctMgr): Approved to proceed with provisional $120 credit. Hold final adj until Ops completes audit. Also offer the 1-week waived burst as goodwill; I'll draft the customer note. :thumbsup:
Emma (Finance): Thanks. Luke — please flag this as "provisional_credit" in billing system and note the root cause as "duplicate_metering_failover_sticky_hashing".
Luke (Billing): On it. Creating credit memo CM-2026-PROV-118. Charging code: credit_note=PROV-ACME-2387.
Sana (CS): I'll add an internal postmortem to eng-ml and tag runtime & metering teams. Need an ops blameless writeup.
Mike (Ops): Uploading full audit csv to the shared bucket: s3://redwood-billing-audits/2026-02/acme-double-count-2387654321.csv
billing-bot: Ticket created: BILL-3627 - "ACME duplicate billing - provisional credit issued" assigned to Luke.
Emma (Finance): One more ask — can someone confirm whether vendor (GCP) metering also reported duplicate samples? If so we should coordinate with vendor.
Mike (Ops): Reached out to cloud-metering@google.com. They confirmed they saw two export records for same VM snapshot due to retried attach; they're investigating.
Nora (AcctMgr): I'll hold off final communication to ACME until vendor confirms. Customer-facing note: "We've applied a provisional credit and are investigating the root cause; we'll follow up within 7 business days with final reconciliation."
Emma (Finance): Perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll mark this thread resolved when Luke confirms credit applied.
Luke (Billing): Credit memo created and applied to INV-2026-0412. final_note: provisional credit $120 applied on 2026-03-10.
Emma (Finance): Confirmed, thank you. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
